scores.Rationale: The proposal addresses an important gap in understanding Lyme disease education and diagnosis in physical therapy. Potential for significant impact on PT curricula and practice is high.

The two-pronged survey approach is well-designed to capture data from educators and clinicians. Timeline is reasonable but ambitious. Some additional details on survey validation and piloting would strengthen the methods.
The PI and co-investigators have complementary expertise well-suited to the project aims. The physician assistant co-investigator adds valuable clinical perspective.
The project lays a strong foundation for a future educational intervention study. Alignment with ILADEF priorities is promising, though more specifics on the envisioned next steps would be helpful.
The budget is appropriate and justified. In-person data collection and participant compensation should enable the study to meet recruitment goals.
The proposal is clearly written and makes a compelling case for the importance and feasibility of the research. Background and impact are especially well-articulated.
